match.reason: The bank point teaches the planning, drafting and editing stages of writing, not how to use feedback from a draft, a model text or classmates to find changes and reflect on what worked, so it is a different idea.

draft.title: Using feedback
card: Feedback shows how a draft compares with what it should be. It can come from the task, a model text or a classmate.
check the draft against the task, or read a good example of the same type of text. Notice how it opens, how it is ordered and which words it chooses.
a classmate reads your draft and says what is clear and what is confusing. They may see problems that you miss.
After you use feedback, reflect. Ask what worked and what to do differently next time. Then change the draft.
draft.remember: Compare your draft with the task, a model or a reader, then reflect on what to change.

a.q: Sam reads a model text about a school trip, then notices his own draft has no clear opening. What is Sam doing?
opts: Comparing his draft with a model text to find a change
Asking a classmate to comment on his draft
Checking his draft against the written task only
Reflecting on what worked after finishing the draft
a.why: Sam is using a model text as feedback. He compares how the model opens with his own draft and sees what to change. He has not asked a classmate, because no one else has read his draft.
a.clue: What did Sam read before he noticed the problem?

b.q: Priya's task is a speech to persuade Year 7 students to join a club. A classmate says her draft sounds like a report. What should Priya do first?
opts: Compare the draft with the task and the form it asks for
Ask the classmate to correct her spelling and punctuation
Decide the comment is wrong because a classmate wrote it
Add more facts to make the draft longer
b.why: The comment suggests the draft may not suit the form the task asks for. Priya should compare it with the task, then change it. Fixing spelling would not solve a problem with form.
b.clue: The comment is about the type of text, not small errors.

a.q: Sam is writing a recount of a school trip. He reads a published recount of another trip and sees it opens with a clear hook. His own draft does not. Which kind of feedback is Sam using?
opts: A good example of the same type of text
A classmate's comments on his draft
The wording of the task he was set
His teacher's comments on the draft
a.why: Sam is using a model text, a good example of the kind of text he is writing. He compares how it opens with his own draft and sees what to change. It is not comments from a classmate or teacher, because no one else has read his draft.
a.clue: What did Sam read before he noticed the problem?
